ai.title: Add unified referral constants and CLI daily session bonus cap
ai.summary: Introduced `MIN_GITHUB_ACCOUNT_AGE_MONTHS_REFERRAL` (12 months) to unify GitHub account-age requirements across all referral programs, replacing the previous split bars of 4 months for Web and 12 months for CLI/GLM. Added `REFERRAL_CLI_DAILY_SESSION_BONUS_CAP` (3) to limit the daily free-mode session bonus granted by qualified limited-tier referrals. These constants in `common/src/constants/freebuff-referral-tiers.ts` support the consolidation of referral logic described in `docs/referrals.md`.

eli5.text: If you refer a friend to the assistant through the Web, desktop app, or browser extension, that friend now needs a GitHub account that's been open for at least a year to qualify for your referral bonus, previously the Web version only required 4 months. Additionally, the number of extra free daily sessions you can earn from these referrals is now capped at 3 per day. These new limits are already in place in the system's core settings, so anyone checking referral requirements will see the updated rules today.

facts: Optional steering hook. Drained at each step boundary (after a step's LLM call + tools complete, before the next one). Any returned texts are appended to the message history as user prompts and keep the turn going, letting a host "steer" a running agent without aborting or losing the current step.

Steering: if the host fed user messages while this step ran, append them now (the step's LLM call + tools have completed, so history is in a clean state) and keep the turn going so the agent responds to them next step, rather than waiting for the whole turn to finish.
entries.title: Agent Runtime update: run-agent-step
entries.summary: Agent Runtime, SDK changes across 2 file(s) (+124/−31).

ai.title: Add optional steering hook to agent runtime loop and SDK run
ai.summary: An optional steering hook (`drainSteeringMessages`) was added to the agent runtime loop and SDK run path, letting a host inject free-text messages into a running agent turn. In `loopAgentSteps`, the hook is drained at each step boundary after a step's LLM call and tools complete; returned strings are appended to `messageHistory` as `USER_PROMPT` user messages and `shouldEndTurn` is forced to false so the agent runs another step. The SDK threads the same option through `RunOptions` into `runOnce` and forwards it to `callMainPrompt`. New tests verify a message appended at the boundary keeps the turn going and that empty returns do not extend the turn.
ai.evidence: Added the optional `drainSteeringMessages?: () => string[]` parameter to `loopAgentSteps` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/run-agent-step.ts` (added to the params type and drained inside the main loop after each `runAgentStep`), and threaded the same option through `RunOptions` into `runOnce` then `callMainPrompt` in `sdk/src/run.ts`, where returned texts are appended to the message history as `USER_PROMPT` user messages and `shouldEndTurn` is forced to false; new tests in `packages/agent-runtime/src/__tests__/loop-agent-steps.test.ts` assert the step boundary message injection and turn continuation.
ai.unknowns: Which host (CLI or web app) currently supplies `drainSteeringMessages` to exercise the hook in practice.

changes.what: Added optional `drainSteeringMessages` parameter to `loopAgentSteps`, drained at step boundaries to append injected user messages and keep the turn going.
Exposed `drainSteeringMessages` on `RunOptions`, destructured it in `runOnce`, and forwarded it to `callMainPrompt`.
Added tests asserting steering messages are appended at the step boundary and continue the turn.

facts: Cap on how much of a failed stdio server's stderr we retain for the error message, enough to show the real failure without unbounded growth.
Buffer the child process's stderr so that a server which crashes during startup produces an actionable error instead of the opaque MCP SDK message "MCP error -32000: Connection closed".
When stderr is 'pipe' the SDK exposes a PassThrough immediately (before the process is spawned), so attaching here captures even early output from a child that dies during the connection handshake.

A failed MCP server (e.g. a stdio server that can't be spawned) should disable just its own tools, not abort the whole turn. The error from the client carries the actionable detail (command + captured stderr).

ai.title: Improve MCP stdio server error handling and isolation
ai.summary: Capture stderr from failed stdio MCP servers (capped at 8KB) to provide actionable errors instead of opaque 'Connection closed' messages. Wrap per-server tool loading in try/catch so a single failed server disables only its own tools without aborting the entire agent turn. Updates common/src/mcp/client.ts and packages/agent-runtime/src/mcp.ts.

eli5.text: The assistant now handles it when one of its outside tools (like a database helper or document reader) quietly fails to start. Instead of stopping everything and showing a confusing message, it will tell you which tool had the problem and why, showing the real reason it couldn't connect rather than just saying the connection closed. You can keep working with your other tools while it figures out what went wrong with the one that failed.

ai.title: Tab completes slash menu without navigating; streak reward constants
ai.summary: Tab and Shift-Tab on the slash menu now accept the highlighted command into the input without executing it (the slash-menu-complete action) instead of cycling through matches, so arrow keys are now the only way to navigate and Enter submits immediately. The change removes the slash-menu-tab and slash-menu-shift-tab actions and their handlers across cli/src/chat.tsx and cli/src/hooks/use-chat-keyboard.ts, and the resolver in cli/src/utils/keyboard-actions.ts returns slash-menu-complete for both key forms, backed by new keyboard-actions tests. The same change introduces streak-reward constants and helpers in common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts and common/src/util/freebuff-streak.ts (interval of 7 days, enabled switches, one session unit per pool, premium/limited/glm pools, milestone detection and pool selection), with streak tests asserting milestone logic, pool assignment, and the off-milestone/before-today null cases.
ai.evidence: In cli/src/utils/keyboard-actions.ts the slash-menu branch maps `isTab || isShiftTab` to `slash-menu-complete` (no longer `slash-menu-tab`/`slash-menu-shift-tab`), and cli/src/chat.tsx removes the `onSlashMenuTab`/`onSlashMenuShiftTab` handlers and their dispatch cases in cli/src/hooks/use-chat-keyboard.ts; new tests assert 'tab completes without executing (does not navigate)', 'shift-tab completes without executing (does not navigate)', 'shift-tab in slash menu completes, not agent mode toggle' in cli/src/utils/__tests__/keyboard-actions.test.ts. Separately, common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts defines FREEBUFF_STREAK_REWARD_INTERVAL_DAYS=7, FREEBUFF_STREAK_REWARDS_ENABLED=true, FREEBUFF_STREAK_GLM_BONUS_ENABLED=true, FREEBUFF_STREAK_BONUS_SESSION_UNITS=1, and the FreebuffStreakRewardPool type plus isFreebuffStreakMilestone and streakRewardPoolsForMilestone (added in common/src/util/freebuff-streak.ts), with tests asserting 'recognizes 7-day multiples as milestones', 'full access milestone grants a premium bonus plus a weekly GLM bonus', 'limited access milestone grants only a limited bonus', 'no reward off a milestone or before today is used' in common/src/util/__tests__/freebuff-streak.test.ts

entries.summary: CLI, Shared/Core changes across 3 file(s) (+106/−4).

ai.title: CLI streak perk note
ai.summary: Added `getFreebuffStreakBonusNote` to display recurring streak rewards on the CLI waiting room when streak >= 7 days. The note accurately reflects active bonuses, showing GLM 5.2 sessions only if `isFreebuffStreakGlmBonusActive` confirms the gate is open. Scope covers `cli/src/components/waiting-room-screen.tsx`, `cli/src/utils/freebuff-streak-line.ts`, and `common/src/util/freebuff-streak.ts`. `streakRewardPoolsForMilestone` now uses the shared active-gate check to prevent granting unusable GLM bonuses when the referral program is disabled.

eli5.text: When you've kept up a 7-day streak (a full week), a short note now appears under the streak counter in the waiting room, telling you that you earn a recurring reward each week you keep the streak going, one extra session, and if you have full access, one GLM session too. The note only shows up once a week is reached and disappears below that, so it doesn't clutter the screen for shorter streaks. It's live today for anyone on the CLI landing screen with a 7+ day streak, and it accurately tracks whether the GLM part is actually available (the extra GLM session only appears if the program is fully enabled, so the note never promises something that can't be used).
